Everis is hiring an early-career analyst to build the pipeline of businesses we may acquire. You will research markets and companies, build relationships with brokers, contact owners, qualify opportunities, do initial analysis, and hand the strongest deals to our acquisition team with clear notes. This is a sourcing and relationship role, not a traditional investment-banking role. Your main responsibility is high-quality deal flow. You will see evaluation, diligence, and transactions, but the deal team owns complex modelling, diligence, negotiation, and execution. Why join Everis Work directly on acquisition strategy and see how a lead becomes a serious opportunity. Speak with brokers, advisers, founders, and owners while learning what makes a business attractive and why owners sell. Research varied industries, use modern AI and sourcing tools, take ownership quickly, and grow into broader acquisition responsibilities. About Everis Everis is an AI-native business group started by successful technology founders. We acquire small internet businesses and apps, improve them, and operate them for the long term. We believe exceptional people, strong systems, and AI can build an unusually effective company. What you’ll work on Broker and intermediary relationships Find and build relationships with relevant brokers, advisers, marketplaces, and other deal sources. Stay in regular contact, understand what they have coming to market, and follow up consistently. Screen brokered and marketplace opportunities against Everis’s criteria and surface the strongest ones quickly. Owner sourcing and outreach Build targeted lists of businesses and owners that may fit our criteria. Find and verify decision-maker contacts, then run thoughtful outreach by phone, email, LinkedIn, referrals, and other relevant channels. Hold initial conversations, understand each owner’s goals, and follow up professionally over what may be a long cycle. Research and qualification Understand what each business does, how it makes money, who its customers are, and what makes it defensible. Gather high-level information on revenue, profit, growth, recurring revenue, customer concentration, owner involvement, asking price, sale motivation, and timing. Assess fit, prepare short opportunity briefs and notes, and coordinate a clean handoff to the deal team. Pipeline ownership and improvement Keep the acquisition CRM accurate, including contacts, source, stage, notes, next action, financial snippets, risks, and follow-up dates. Track outreach, responses, meetings, qualified opportunities, handoffs, and funnel progression. Provide concise weekly reporting. Use evidence and AI tools to improve research, outreach, recordkeeping, and the sourcing methods that produce the best opportunities. What we’re looking for Smart, curious, and able to understand unfamiliar businesses quickly. Excellent spoken and written communication; you can sound credible with experienced brokers and owners without finance jargon. Comfortable making cold calls, sending outbound messages, hearing no, and following up. Highly organized and reliable, with accurate notes and strong follow-through. Strong research judgment and basic financial and commercial literacy, or the ability to learn quickly. High integrity and care with confidential information. Comfortable with spreadsheets, CRM systems, research databases, and AI tools. Motivated, proactive, resilient, and able to work without constant supervision. Zero to three years of professional experience. Relevant sourcing, sales, research, brokerage, consulting, or entrepreneurial experience is useful but not required. What we offer US$70,000–$85,000 base salary plus an annual performance bonus of up to US$15,000. 100% remote work from the United States or Canada. Direct exposure to founders, brokers, owners, and real acquisition opportunities. Meaningful responsibility early, with a path into senior deal origination, acquisitions, or broader operating work. If you want to learn how great businesses are found and directly help build Everis’s acquisition pipeline, we’d like to hear from youHelp me write the role description.

review_candidates.title: Clinical Care Facilitator, Community Acquired Pneumonia (Integrated Care Pathway)
review_candidates.description: BACKGROUND Community Acquired Pneumonia Pathway The East Toronto Care Network (EastTCaN) Community Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) Integrated Care Pathway supports adults transitioning from Michael Garron Hospital to recovery at home. The pathway brings together hospital, primary care, home care and community providers to support transitions, strengthen patient and caregiver confidence, and reduce avoidable emergency department visits and readmissions. Working collaboratively with MGH2Home (homecare support), the pathway combines individualized recovery planning, education, structured clinical follow-up and access to the MGH2Home respiratory bundle for eligible patients. An initial two-week period of supported recovery focuses on recognizing deterioration, addressing recovery needs and connecting patients with ongoing care. POSITION OVERVIEW The Clinical Care Facilitator (CCF) is a core member of the CAP interdisciplinary team and the primary point of contact for enrolled patients during their transition from hospital to home. The CCF conducts assessments within their professional scope, develops individualized recovery plans, provides evidence-informed education and structured clinical follow-up, coordinates care with MGH2Home, primarycare, physicians and community partners. Working in partnership with patients and caregivers, the CCF monitors recovery, addresses barriers and supports progress toward recovery. This position is open to a Nurse Practitioner, Physician Assistant, Registered Nurse or Registered Respiratory Therapist. Clinical responsibilities will be aligned with the successful candidate’s professional scope, demonstrated competencies and organizational policies, including applicable orders, medical directives and physician supervision or delegation arrangements. The role includes access to designated medical support and clear escalation processes. Primary Responsibilities Clinical Assessment and Recovery Support Work with Access and Flow and inpatient teams to review referrals, confirm pathway eligibility and engage patients before discharge. Review admission risk information, including CRB-65, and documented discharge stability assessments to inform recovery planning and follow-up needs. Conduct initial and ongoing assessments within professional scope, including respiratory symptoms, recovery trajectory, functional ability and relevant clinical findings. Identify concerns related to oxygen needs, medication adherence, hydration, nutrition, cognition, frailty, caregiver capacity and the ability to manage safely at home. Develop individualized recovery plans and achievable goals with patients and caregivers. Provide structured telephone, video or in-person follow-up according to patient needs and the approved pathway. Recognize deterioration or unexpected recovery and arrange timely clinical review using established escalation protocols. Provide clinical interventions within authorized scope and seek appropriate medical or interdisciplinary input for needs requiring additional expertise. Support transition to primary care, community services or another EastTCaN pathway when ongoing needs are identified. Patient and Caregiver Education Build therapeutic relationships with patients and caregivers during hospitalization and throughout recovery. Explain expected pneumonia recovery, treatment plans, warning signs and how to access help. Use teach-back and coaching to strengthen understanding, confidence and self-management. Review the medication plan, identify discrepancies or concerns, and collaborate with the appropriate prescriber or pharmacist to resolve them. Reinforce antibiotic adherence, safe activity progression, nutrition and hydration recommendations tailored to the patient’s clinical needs. Provide respiratory education, including inhaler technique, oxygen safety and smoking cessation support, within professional competencies. Identify language, accessibility, technology and social barriers and arrange appropriate supports. Care Coordination and MGH2Home Collaboration Coordinate with MGH2Home to support assessment for the respiratory bundle and confirm services for patients enrolled in both programs. Develop one coordinated recovery plan that clearly outlines clinical follow-up, home services, patient goals and escalation contacts. Participate in joint patient reviews with MGH2Home and communicate with home care providers about recovery progress and emerging concerns. Clarify responsibilities across the inpatient, ICP and home care teams to support continuity and avoid duplication. Facilitate primary care follow-up and communicate relevant recovery information to the ongoing care team. Coordinate referrals to rehabilitation, nutrition, pharmacy, social work, Ontario Health atHome and other services as needed. Support continuity when MGH2Home services end or patients require additional community care. Interdisciplinary Practice and Clinical Escalation Collaborate with designated physicians, NP/PA colleagues and other interdisciplinary providers to address clinical concerns. Apply approved escalation protocols and communicate relevant assessment findings promptly. Arrange urgent or emergency assessment when indicated. Participate in interdisciplinary rounds and care planning discussions. Maintain timely, accurate clinical documentation and communicate care decisions and follow-up responsibilities. Program Development and Evaluation Use current evidence-based research and clinical guidelines to inform pathway development, care delivery and ongoing improvement, working with clinical leads to translate findings into practice. Support development of assessment tools, patient education materials, recovery plans and communication processes. Support evaluation of enrollment, follow-up completion, patient and caregiver experience, recovery outcomes and acute care utilization. Identify service gaps and recommend improvements that strengthen safety, equity and coordination. EDUCATION Applicants must meet the requirements for one of the following professions: Nurse Practitioner: Current registration as a Nurse Practitioner (RN-EC) in good standing with the College of Nurses of Ontario (CNO), with Adult or Primary Health Care specialty. Physician Assistant: Current registration in good standing with the College of Physicians and Surgeons of Ontario as a Physician Assistant. Registered Nurse: Current registration in good standing with the College of Nurses of Ontario as a Registered Nurse. Registered Respiratory Therapist: Current registration in good standing with the College of Respiratory Therapists of Ontario. Experience Minimum two years of relevant clinical experience in respiratory care, acute medicine, older adult care, complex chronic disease management or community care. Demonstrated assessment and clinical reasoning skills appropriate to professional scope, including recognition of deterioration and timely escalation. Experience supporting transitions from hospital to home and collaborating across care settings. Experience working with older adults with frailty, multiple conditions or complex recovery needs. Strong patient and caregiver education skills, including teach-back and self-management support. Ability to manage a caseload, prioritize competing needs and work independently within an interdisciplinary team. Strong communication, relationship-building and documentation skills. Familiarity with electronic medical records and willingness to use program documentation and evaluation tools. Knowledge of community resources and experience in care coordination or case management are assets. Experience in quality improvement or implementation of a new clinical service is an asset. All employees of Michael Garron Hospital (MGH), a division of Toronto East Health Network (TEHN) [formerly Toronto East General Hospital (TEGH)] agree to work within the legislated practices of the Occupational Health and Safety Act of Ontario All employees of MGH are responsible to contribute to a transparent culture of patient and staff safety by adhering to and a biding by patient and staff safety policies and procedures set by MGH All employees are accountable for protecting the psychological health and safety of themselves and their co-workers through adherence to MGH's policies and practices. What You Bring A commitment to person-centred care, health equity and recovery at home. Sound professional judgment and an understanding of when to seek additional expertise. A collaborative approach to working with patients, caregivers and partners across organizations. Flexibility and initiative to help develop and improve a new integrated care pathway EMPLOYMENT EQUITY & ACCESSIBILITY STATEMENT Michael Garron Hospital (MGH) champions accessibility, diversity and equal opportunity through the creation of an inclusive and diverse work environment. review_candidates.title: Advanced Operator
review_candidates.description: Who We Are Zinfra is a leading partner in the design, build, operation and maintenance of Australia’s energy and utilities infrastructure. Delivering an annual portfolio of more than $1.2 billion, our work helps keep energy flowing safely and reliably to communities across Australia while supporting the nation’s energy transition. With a workforce of more than 2,800 people, we deliver complex infrastructure, asset management and field services across Australia’s east coast. Our people draw on deep industry experience, an unwavering commitment to safety, and practical innovation to deliver the right outcomes for our clients and communities. About The Role Join our high performing civil construction crews as an Advanced Plant Operator out of our Heathwood depot and play a hands-on role in delivering essential infrastructure. You’ll take on varied work across excavation, backfilling, cable installation including underground fibre optics, recoveries and reinstatement. This field-based opportunity will see you working alongside a skilled, multidisciplinary team on projects where no two days are the same. You’ll build your experience across a broad range of activities, take on meaningful responsibility and stay challenged in a fast-paced, supportive environment. Standard working hours: 6:00am to 4:00pm, Monday to Friday Excavate trenches according to specifications and install pipe as per plans Shovel materials like asphalt and dirt to and from construction site Load and unload construction materials and supplies from trucks Keep the work site organised, safe, and running smoothly, including machinery and work sites Operate a variety of hand and power tools and assist with underground service spotting Read and interpret plans and take direction from the Crew Leader About You The successful applicant will have experience working in a similar role within the construction industry, while actively participating in identifying site hazards and implementing control measures. Proven experience operating excavators, with a strong knowledge of trenching techniques and the ability to dig around underground services Ability to implement environmental controls and read and interpret DBYD plans Current HR Driver’s Licence Excavators and Skid Steer tickets First Aid, Dogging, and Confined Space tickets are highly desirable Why Work With Us We know Zinfra is a great place to belong – but don’t just take our word for it. Hear directly from our people about what it's like to build a career, make an impact and be part of the team at Zinfra. We champion and value diversity in life and work experiences, because broader perspectives strengthen our problem solving, decision making and ability to innovate. We welcome applications from everyone, including First Nations peoples, veterans, people living with disability and members of the LGBTIQA+ community. If you require adjustments during the recruitment process, please let us know. Recruitment Process During the recruitment process, you may be required to undertake pre-employment checks, including a pre-employment medical, reference checks and a national police check. Notice to Third Parties Zinfra does not accept unsolicited resumes, or liability associated with fees or costs, from recruitment agencies, search firms or other third parties. Interested candidates are welcome to submit their application independently.
